stories.headline: US Envoys Kushner and Witkoff Visit Kyiv for Peace Talks
stories.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Kyiv for peace talks. This was their first visit to Kyiv since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky greeted Witkoff and Kushner at Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv. On Friday, Russian drones hit the headquarters of Ukraine's security services near that cathedral. Russian strikes also bombed the two main airports in Kyiv on Friday. Those strikes forced Kushner and Witkoff to travel to the capital city by train. They travelled by train because of the risk of Russian drone strikes.

Russia and Ukraine agreed to a short-term pause in air strikes during the visit. Both countries pledged not to attack each other's capitals over the weekend. They made this pledge to ensure safe passage for the US envoys. Before arriving in Ukraine, Kushner and Witkoff spent time in Moscow. They held three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday. Putin told the envoys that Russia was making tangible advances on the battlefield.

After the talks in Moscow, the envoys went to Kyiv. Witkoff said that peace talks in Ukraine have been very meaningful. UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell joined the talks in Kyiv. Other European national security advisers also participated in the discussions. The talks have focused on a 20-point peace plan. Washington and Kyiv put forward this peace plan in December.

Zelensky said that Ukraine is counting on a winter package from the US and Europe. He said this package needs to include air defence. He said it must also include energy support. He added that the package should include American LNG.

While diplomats met, attacks continued in other areas. Ukrainian authorities reported on Sunday that at least eight people were killed across the country in the past day. They reported that 69 people were injured during the same period. Ukraine also reported that its forces struck the Ryazan oil refinery overnight. That refinery is about 480 kilometres inside Russia. The strike caused a fire at the refinery.

Ukrainian officials also made claims about the war in August. They claimed that Russia suffered 42,000 dead or wounded casualties during August. They also claimed that Ukraine gained more territory than it lost that month.

stories.headline: Amazon Cargo Plane Crashes at Miami Airport Killing At Least Five
stories.body:
An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, killing at least five people. Five other people were injured in the crash. The flight was arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed that 21 Air Flight 7598 overran the runway around 2 pm local time on September 6. The aircraft was a Boeing 767-300 cargo plane. It overshot the runway and struck several vehicles.

Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said five people died and five were injured. More than 60 units from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the scene. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the agency issued a full ground stop in Miami after the crash. All runways and taxiways at the airport were closed by 3 pm. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office closed NW 67th Avenue between NW 25th Street and NW 36th Street. Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said there was no apparent threat to public safety.

The Boeing 767-300 aircraft was over 32 years old. It first flew in June 1994 as a passenger aircraft. Cargo carrier 21 Air began operating Boeing 767-300 freighters for Amazon in 2024.

stories.headline: Far-Right AfD Wins Record Share in Saxony-Anhalt Election
stories.body:
The far-right Alternative for Germany party won a record vote share in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Incomplete results show the party, known as AfD, set to win 44% of the vote. Voter turnout in the state was estimated at 78%. Saxony-Anhalt has a population of 2.1 million people. Domestic intelligence classifies the state branch of AfD as right-wing extremist. AfD state leader Ulrich Siegmund called the result sensational.

The conservative CDU finished second with just over 17% of the vote. CDU national general secretary Franziska Hoppermann called the result very difficult for her party. She rejected any cooperation with the AfD. Exit polls showed Die Linke won 9.3%. The Social Democrats won 8.4%, and the Greens won 8.7%. The BSW party reached the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament.

Modern Germany has never had a far-right party lead a state government since World War II. Siegmund promised to launch a remigration and deportation offensive if AfD forms a government. He also promised to ban rainbow flags in schools. In addition, he promised to stop new windfarm construction.

stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Warnings and Attacks in Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the United States will sink Iranian oil tankers if Iran attacks American ships. He said the US will destroy those tankers if Iran shoots at US vessels. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Americans must understand that the rules of the game have changed before it is too late. The conflict between the countries started on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks on Iran.

Iran claimed it struck an unmanned American vessel near the Strait of Hormuz. The US denied this claim and called the allegation a total lie. A report by the New York Times said August was the deadliest month for merchant ships near the Strait of Hormuz since March. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on CNN that about 9 million barrels of oil a day currently pass through the strait.

Wright said on ABC that a nuclear agreement with Iran may not be reached. He said the US is degrading Iran's ability to develop and deliver nuclear weapons. In the US, the average price for one gallon of diesel reached $5.85 on Friday.

stories.headline: Anak Krakatau Eruption Disrupts Flights Across Indonesia
stories.body:
Volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau forced officials to suspend over 300 flights at Jakarta's main airport on Sunday. That airport was Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. Two new eruptions occurred as the volcano spewed ash across the region. Indonesian authorities suspended operations at eight airports. The closures left about 170,000 passengers stranded. The Indonesian transport ministry reported that 1,558 flights were delayed.

Volcanic ash reached up to 20,000 feet on the Java side. The ash reached 50,000 feet on the Sumatra side. Booming sounds from the eruption were heard up to 435 miles or 700 kilometres away. Indonesia's disaster agency BNPB announced plans for cloud-seeding to wash away the ash. Port authorities banned ships in the Sunda Strait from going within two miles of the volcano.

Indonesian authorities confirmed that no tsunami warning is active for this eruption. A previous eruption and collapse of Anak Krakatau in 2018 triggered a tsunami that killed more than 400 people.

stories.headline: Building Collapse Kills At Least Five in Delhi's Satya Niketan
stories.body:
A five-storey building housing college students collapsed in South West Delhi on September 6, 2026. The building was located in the Satya Niketan area. Satya Niketan is a dense hub for paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus. Eyewitnesses told local media that up to 50 people were inside the building when it collapsed at around 13:30 local time on Sunday. At least five people were killed in the disaster. Reports differed on the number of survivors rescued from the site. The Hindu reported that 11 people were pulled out and taken to the hospital. Al Jazeera reported that nine people were rescued.

Residents said the collapsed building was at least 50 years old. They said the structure comprised a basement plus five upper floors. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi said the building violated building norms. Municipal rules permitted only a ground floor plus a first floor. Repair work was underway in the basement when the collapse happened. A local shop owner said the leaseholder was conducting excavation work in the basement to expand the hostel.

Police launched legal action against multiple individuals associated with the property. Delhi Police said they are registering a first information report against Anand Bansal. Bansal operates the Hostel Daze paying guest accommodation. Deputy Commissioner of Police Amit Goel said an FIR was registered against building owner Hariram and others at the South Campus police station.

Authorities also took action regarding neighboring properties and ordered an official inquiry. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi evacuated tenants from an adjoining girls' paying guest building and sealed that property. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered a magisterial probe into the collapse.

The collapse sparked student demonstrations in the city. Around 150 to 200 members of the ABVP student organization protested at Delhi's Civic Centre. They demonstrated against the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. A security guard was injured when protesters tried to force their way into the main Civic Centre building. Delhi Police detained around 15 students after the protest. Police initiated legal proceedings against them under the Delhi Police Act.

Building safety remains a persistent issue in the Indian capital. Fire department figures show that more than 1,000 building collapses occurred in Delhi over the past three years. In April, 11 people were killed when a residential building collapsed in north-eastern Delhi.

stories.headline: ISRO and IN-SPACe Reject Reports of Space Agency Privatisation
stories.body:
The Indian Space Research Organisation rejected reports that it will be privatised or its role reduced. The agency, known as ISRO, called those reports baseless and incorrect. IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka said ISRO will remain the bedrock of the space sector and lead next-generation programmes. ISRO said strategic and nationally critical capabilities will remain under government ownership.

Nine ISRO employee associations sent a joint letter on September 4 to ISRO Chairperson V. Narayanan. They asked for official clarification on plans to transfer manufacturing to private companies. The letter was signed by groups including the ISRO Staff Association, SHAR Employees Association, and ISAC Employees Association. The associations cited remarks by Goenka that ISRO would eventually not manufacture launch vehicles. They wrote that reducing ISRO to a residual research unit cannot be accepted without debate. Department of Space employees are organized as service associations rather than trade unions.

India aims to grow its space economy from about $8.4 billion to $44 billion by 2033. The country currently has more than 450 space startups. India targets 50 space launches a year by 2030. Space goals include establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and sending a crewed mission to the Moon by 2040. On September 4, ISRO launched its EOS-05 Earth imaging satellite aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket. Private company Skyroot launched its Vikram-1 rocket on July 18.
